L0: # API Overview
L1: 
L2: A2A Superhub exposes a compact JSON API plus a minimal JSON-RPC A2A facade.
L3: This file documents the coordination runtime and opt-in durable-memory,
L4: offline-sharing, hybrid-retrieval, and optional artifact-text derivation foundations.
L5: Memory v2 is the current agent-facing contract; the complete route and payload
L6: contract is in [MEMORY_API.md](MEMORY_API.md). The delivery migration,
L7: compatibility window, and rollback boundary are in
L8: [MEMORY_V2_COMPATIBILITY.md](MEMORY_V2_COMPATIBILITY.md). Inbox, wakeup,
L9: task-log sedimentation, the reference adapter, operator Skill, and MCP stdio
L10: sidecar are implemented. An A2A 1.0 runtime binding remains absent.
L11: ## Public endpoints
L12: 
L13: These endpoints are available without bearer auth:
L14: 
L15: - `GET /healthz`
L16: - `GET /readyz`
L17: - `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json`
L18: 
L19: ## Authenticated endpoints
L20: 
L21: If `--token` or `A2A_SUPERHUB_TOKEN` is configured, all `/v1/*`, `/v2/*`, and
L22: `/a2a` requests require `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
L23: 
L24: Non-loopback binds fail at startup unless a legacy token or static principal
L25: registry is configured. Loopback no-token mode resolves to `local.operator`.
L26: ## Opt-in memory and retrieval foundation
L27: 
L28: Install `.[memory-core]` and run `serve --enable-memory`. The default remains
L29: off. New agents should negotiate `GET /v2/capabilities` and use `/v2/memory/*`.
L30: Version 0.3.x also writes and serves the v1 per-reason delivery projection so
L31: existing v1 consumers continue to work during the documented compatibility
L32: window.
L33: - `POST /v2/memory/notes` creates an immutable Markdown note. Supply a 1–128
L34:   character idempotency key in `Idempotency-Key` or `idempotencyKey`; author,
L35:   source, and recorded time are server-derived. Relation targets must use
L36:   `agent:`, `note:`, `project:`, `task:`, `event:`, or `artifact:`.
L37: - `GET /v2/memory/notes/<id>` reads only after final authorization against the
L38:   current Markdown frontmatter. Add `includeLifecycle=true`, or request
L39:   `/v2/memory/notes/<id>/lifecycle`, for authorized operational facts.
L40: - `GET /v2/memory/notes?limit=...` lists authorized note summaries.
L41: - `GET /v2/memory/search?q=...&limit=...&mode=auto|hybrid|keyword` performs
L42:   authorized hybrid retrieval when configured and retains FTS-compatible
L43:   keyword fallback.
L44: - `GET /v2/capabilities` reports the `logical.v2` delivery model,
L45:   `ackCursorSource: inbox-only`, `wakeupAckMode: none`, lifecycle availability,
L46:   and granular runtime features. `memoryFull` remains false.
L47: One v2 inbox item represents one logical delivery identified by note and
L48: recipient. If several routing rules match, the item contains the complete
L49: bounded `reasons` array (`about`, `direct`, and/or `handoff`) instead of
L50: duplicating the content. Within v2, only `/v2/memory/inbox` issues an
L51: acknowledgeable cursor, recorded with the exact delivery IDs returned on that
L52: page. Wakeup is a bounded untrusted preview: it never returns a cursor and
L53: never authorizes an ACK. Acknowledge an inbox cursor only after that exact page
L54: was accepted by the intended consumer.
L55: Lifecycle output is an authorization-filtered set of stored, indexed, queued,
L56: acknowledged, and linked-reference facts. It is not a linear state and does not
L57: claim that another agent understood or executed the note.
L58: The same opt-in runtime provides durable multi-consumer inbox fetch/ack, safe
L59: wakeup, timeline/graph, sanitized stats/receipts, and allowlisted task-log
L60: replay. Errors use a typed safe envelope with `code`, `message`, `retryable`,
L61: optional bounded validation `details`, and `traceId`; the HTTP client and MCP
L62: sidecar preserve these fields. See [MEMORY_API.md](MEMORY_API.md) for scopes,
L63: schemas, and compatibility behavior.
L64: CLI support covers note create/read, reindex, inbox fetch/ack, wakeup,
L65: timeline/graph, and stats. The separate `skill` commands expose path,
L66: validation, contained install, and ownership-aware uninstall. Reindex builds a
L67: new derived-index generation and atomically swaps it; it never rebuilds or
L68: deletes the ops database.
L69: ## Operational diagnostics and local controls
L70: `GET /v1/operations/diagnostics` requires `hub.admin` and returns the
L71: `a2a-superhub.operations-diagnostics.v1` payload-free view: store counts,
L72: pending queue/outbox and quarantine counts, source/index revision, retrieval
L73: model identity, product version, and aggregate state bytes. It never returns
L74: task payloads, note bodies, token material, or local paths. Only one full
L75: diagnostic refresh runs at a time. While it runs, concurrent requests receive
L76: the last completed snapshot, with its original `generatedAt` value, instead of
L77: starting duplicate corpus scans. A caller can therefore detect an unchanged
L78: snapshot without confusing it with newly collected state.
L79: Authoritative backup/clean restore, recoverable retention, and Qdrant migration
L80: are intentionally local CLI operations, not remote mutation endpoints. The
L81: running hub holds a state lease, so these commands fail closed until it is
L82: stopped. Their machine contracts are in `schemas/operations-v1.schema.json` and
L83: operator procedures are in [OPERATIONS.md](OPERATIONS.md).
L84: ## MCP sidecar
L85: 
L86: Install `.[mcp]` and launch `a2a-superhub-mcp`. The sidecar reads
L87: `A2A_SUPERHUB_URL` and `A2A_SUPERHUB_TOKEN`, speaks MCP `2025-11-25` over stdio,
L88: and delegates every operation to these HTTP endpoints. It exposes ten tools:
L89: `memory_write`, `memory_search`, `memory_read`, `memory_timeline`,
L90: `memory_graph`, `memory_wakeup`, `memory_inbox`, `memory_inbox_ack`,
L91: `task_create`, and `task_status`.
L92: The sidecar uses memory v2. `memory_read` accepts `includeLifecycle`; inbox
L93: items use logical deliveries and reason arrays; `memory_wakeup` remains a
L94: cursor-free preview; and `memory_inbox_ack` accepts only a cursor issued by
L95: `memory_inbox`.
L96: `memory://note/{id}` and `memory://wakeup/{agent}` are authorized JSON resources.
L97: The sidecar advertises resource subscriptions and emits updated notifications
L98: when the underlying HTTP view changes. Clients without subscription support
L99: poll `resources/read`. Tool annotations describe effects but never replace hub
L100: authentication, scopes, current visibility checks, or idempotency.
L101: ## Agents
L102: 
L103: ### `POST /v1/agents/register`
L104: 
L105: Registers an Agent Card. The request body may be the card itself or `{ "card": ... }`.
L106: The card must contain `id` or `name`.
L107: 
L108: ### `GET /v1/agents`
L109: 
L110: Lists registered Agent Cards.
L111: 
L112: ## Tasks
L113: ### `POST /v1/tasks`
L114: 
L115: Creates a task. Required fields:
L116: 
L117: - `fromAgent`
L118: - `toAgent`
L119: 
L120: Common fields:
L121: 
L122: - `intent`
L123: - `idempotencyKey`
L124: - `payload`
L125: - `artifactRefs`
L126: - `permissions`
L127: - `limits`
L128: - `correlation`
L129: 
L130: Duplicate `idempotencyKey` values return the existing task instead of inserting a
L131: new one.
L132: 
L133: ### `GET /v1/tasks`
L134: 
L135: Lists recent tasks. Optional query: `limit`.
L136: 
L137: ### `GET /v1/tasks/<task-id>`
L138: 
L139: Returns a task.
L140: ### `POST /v1/tasks/<task-id>/events`
L141: 
L142: Appends an event. Body fields:
L143: 
L144: - `kind`, default `task.progress`
L145: - `payload`, default `{}`
L146: - `state`, optional task state update
L147: 
L148: ### `GET /v1/tasks/<task-id>/events`
L149: 
L150: Lists task events.
L151: 
L152: ### `POST /v1/tasks/<task-id>/cancel`
L153: 
L154: Records a cancellation event and moves the task to `canceled`.
L155: ## Artifacts
L156: 
L157: The authenticated principal is the artifact owner. Reads/lists require
L158: `artifact.read`; writes require `artifact.write`; shared/direct visibility also
L159: requires `artifact.share`. Details and examples are in
L160: [ARTIFACTS_AND_DERIVATION.md](ARTIFACTS_AND_DERIVATION.md).
L161: ### `POST /v1/artifacts`
L162: 
L163: Stores a base64 artifact.
L164: 
L165: Required field:
L166: 
L167: - `contentBase64`
L168: 
L169: Optional fields:
L170: 
L171: - `filename`
L172: - `mediaType`
L173: - `visibility`
L174: - `sha256`
L175: - `policy`
L176: 
L177: Any `createdBy` field is ignored; ownership is server-derived.
L178: 
L179: ### `PUT /v1/artifacts/raw`
L180: 
L181: Streams a binary artifact with `Content-Length`, `Content-Type`, optional
L182: filename/visibility headers, and an optional expected SHA-256.
L183: ### `POST /v1/artifacts/chunks`
L184:

L0: # Artifact Transport and Searchable Derived Text
L1: 
L2: A2A Superhub stores artifact bytes in a SHA-256 content-addressed store. The
L3: manifest and blob are authoritative; derived Markdown and search indexes are
L4: rebuildable outputs. The default maximum artifact size is 64 MiB and can be
L5: changed with `serve --max-artifact-bytes`.
L6: ## Enable the optional derivers
L7: 
L8: ```bash
L9: python -m pip install -e ".[memory-core,derive]"
L10: a2a-superhub --state ./state serve --enable-memory --enable-derivers
L11: ```
L12: 
L13: Derivers are off by default. PDF text extraction runs locally through `pypdf`.
L14: Image OCR validates/decompresses through Pillow, then invokes a separately
L15: installed `tesseract` executable with an argument-safe subprocess and timeout.
L16: Provider absence is reported as an error; the hub does not silently send media
L17: to a cloud API.
L18: ## Complete raw upload
L19: 
L20: `PUT /v1/artifacts/raw` accepts a binary body with:
L21: 
L22: - `Content-Length` (required);
L23: - `Content-Type`;
L24: - `X-Artifact-SHA256` (recommended and verified when present);
L25: - `X-Artifact-Filename`;
L26: - `X-Artifact-Visibility`: `private`, `shared`, or `direct:<principal>`.
L27: The authenticated principal becomes `createdBy`; client-provided ownership is
L28: never trusted. A temporary file is flushed and checksum-verified before the blob
L29: and manifest become visible. Size or checksum failure removes the partial file.
L30: Legacy manifests without an explicit visibility field are treated as private.
L31: Static principal registries must grant `artifact.share` before a caller can
L32: create or change shared/direct artifacts; legacy single-token mode already maps
L33: to the complete local-operator scope set.
L34: ## Restart-safe resumable upload
L35: 
L36: 1. `POST /v1/artifacts/chunks` with `sizeBytes`, `chunkSize`, `sha256`, optional
L37:    filename/media type, and visibility.
L38: 2. `PUT /v1/artifacts/chunks/<upload-id>/<zero-based-index>` with the exact chunk
L39:    bytes and optional `X-Chunk-SHA256`.
L40: 3. `POST /v1/artifacts/chunks/<upload-id>/commit` with `{}`.
L41: Chunks may arrive out of order. Repeating identical bytes at an index is
L42: idempotent; different bytes at the same index are a conflict. Commit fails while
L43: any chunk is missing and verifies the whole-file checksum before CAS admission.
L44: Session metadata survives a server restart. Explicit
L45: `POST /v1/artifacts/chunks/<upload-id>/cancel` removes partial chunks while
L46: retaining a canceled status record.
L47: The JSON `POST /v1/artifacts` base64 route remains available for compatibility,
L48: but raw or resumable upload avoids base64 expansion.
L49: ## A2A Part mapping
L50: 
L51: Message parts accept the official oneof member names `text`, `raw`, `url`, and
L52: `data`; exactly one must be present. `raw` is strict base64. Raw parts larger
L53: than 256 KiB become private CAS URL references and require `artifact.write`.
L54: The old `kind` discriminator is accepted only when the caller explicitly opts
L55: into legacy mapping. This implements Part validation/mapping, not the complete
L56: A2A 1.0 JSON-RPC binding.
L57: ## Derive, search, and retrieve
L58: 
L59: `POST /v1/artifacts/<artifact-id>/derive` with `{}` chooses the registered
L60: provider by media type. The durable job can be read at
L61: `GET /v1/derivations/<job-id>`. A failed or canceled job requires
L62: `{"retry": true}` to retry. The resulting Markdown note includes:
L63: 
L64: - an `UNTRUSTED DERIVED DATA` boundary;
L65: - source artifact ID and authoritative checksum;
L66: - provider name/version and media type;
L67: - an `x-derived-from` backlink plus the checksum reference.
L68: The extracted text remains data even when it contains phrases such as “ignore
L69: previous instructions.” Adapters and the operator Skill must never promote it
L70: to a system or developer role.
L71: 
L72: The derived note initially inherits the source visibility. Every note read and
L73: search hydration checks the current source manifest again, so narrowing a source
L74: from shared to private immediately hides stale derived search candidates. A
L75: missing or inconsistent manifest fails closed.
L76: ## Cancel and rollback
L77: 
L78: `POST /v1/derivations/<job-id>/cancel` cancels a pending/running job. Provider
L79: timeouts and output limits bound work; cancellation may complete at the next
L80: provider boundary rather than interrupting a native process instantly.
L81: `POST /v1/derivations/<job-id>/purge` is an admin-only destructive operation.
L82: It removes only the derived Markdown note and rebuildable index entries. It does
L83: not delete or mutate the source manifest/blob. The product exposes no general
L84: source-artifact deletion endpoint.
L85: ## Verification and limitations
L86: Repository scenarios cover raw and out-of-order resumable transport, duplicate
L87: and missing chunks, checksum mismatch, restart/replay, explicit cancel, valid and
L88: encrypted/malformed/oversized PDF handling, malformed/oversized images, real
L89: Tesseract OCR when the provider exists, prompt-like text containment, cross-
L90: principal search, current-ACL denial, default-off behavior, and derived-only
L91: cleanup. These are repository and CI outcomes, not production deployment, load,
L92: latency, or soak claims. Image captioning, audio/video transcription, general
L93: artifact garbage collection, and the complete A2A 1.0 binding are not implemented.
